assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: yes
daemon_capability: full
driver_capability: ready

## agent — yes

A single no-tool round-trip is Hermes' base case, and the live store already contains one verbatim: session `20260802_212608_1dc71a` (`source='cli'`, model `gpt-5.6-luna`) holds exactly two message rows — `role='user'` "Say only: beta" followed by `role='assistant' finish_reason='stop'` "beta" — with `input_tokens=16269`, `output_tokens=5`, `message_count=2` on its `sessions` row. Across the whole store there are 29 `assistant/finish_reason='stop'` rows. Binary is `hermes` v0.19.0 (2026.7.20) on PATH. No search was needed for a hidden surface: the behavior is present in captured data.

## daemon — full

The two user-observable signals the scenario asserts map onto events this adapter produces today:

1. **`ready → working → ready`.** `Watcher.reconcile` emits `EventNewSession` on first sight of a `sessions` row and an `EventActivity` whenever `message_count` grows, with `Terminal` set from `turnIsDone` — which reads the newest `active=1` row and returns true only for `role='assistant' AND finish_reason='stop'`. `Parser.ParseLine` maps `role='user'` → `user_message` (clears open tools) and `role='assistant' + finish_reason='stop'` → `turn_done`. Hermes' `finish_reason` is an EXPLICIT turn boundary, so no idle-flush heuristic sits between the agent and the `ready` settle — the one structural way a basic-turn arc usually degrades is absent here.
2. **`TotalTokens > 0`.** `querySessionMetrics` reads `input_tokens`/`output_tokens`/`cache_read_tokens`/`cache_write_tokens` off the `sessions` aggregate and sets `TotalTokens = input + output`; the live store shows these are populated (16269/5 on the minimal session above). Cost is priced through irrlicht's own alias table rather than `sessions.estimated_cost_usd` (Hermes reports 0.0 under `billing_mode='subscription_included'`), which is the repo convention.

Both watcher and `processlifecycle` scanner are wired for this adapter at `core/cmd/irrlichd/wiring.go:90` / `:102`, so a launched `hermes chat` is seen as a process before its store row exists.

### The one shape that makes this cell different from its siblings

Hermes' `sessions` row is INSERTed on the FIRST USER MESSAGE (~2s after launch), not at launch — so the store yields no launch-time `ready` birth. The `ready` birth in a recording comes from the scanner's transient `proc-<PID>` pre-session, which the real session then supersedes (`cleanupPreSessionsForProject`). That is the same situation `opencode` documents for this scenario, so the spec uses the same anchoring: `session_birth` anchored to `start` and left UNPINNED, `turn1_done` chained to `turn1_start` via `same_session_as`. It is an anchoring consequence, not an observability gap — hence `full` with a caveat rather than a downgrade.

## driver — ready

`replaydata/agents/hermes/driver-interactive.sh` declares `DRIVE_ELICITS="send slash sleep wait_turn"`, and this recipe needs only `send` + `wait_turn` + `sleep`. Its `wait_turn` is a real signal poll, not an idle guess: it counts `messages` rows with `role='assistant' AND finish_reason='stop'` for the bound session and returns when the count increases. `resolve_session_id` binds only to a session with `started_at >` the slot's launch timestamp, so a leftover row in the shared store cannot satisfy the wait. The interactive (`hermes chat`) path is the right one for this arc: the REPL outlives the turn, so the settle to `ready` falls inside the observation window instead of racing process exit.

## What is NOT proven yet

Everything above is code + live-store evidence; no recording exists. Under the observation-vs-emission rule the `daemon=full` verdict is PROVISIONAL on the arc actually reaching the websocket — `record` promotes it.
caveats: PROVISIONAL daemon verdict: derived from the adapter source plus live SQLite store facts, not from a recording. No hermes events.jsonl exists yet; record settles whether the arc reaches the websocket.

Late birth: the sessions row is INSERTed on the first user message (~2s after launch, adapter.go:16-19), so no store-derived ready birth exists at launch. The recording's ready birth comes from the processlifecycle scanner's proc-<PID> pre-session; session_birth is therefore anchored to start and left UNPINNED and turn1_done chains off turn1_start (the opencode shape).

cwd fragility: `hermes chat` records source='cli', and CLI rows carry no cwd (live store: 21 of 22 cli rows have an empty cwd; 0 of 3 tui rows do). Both the project binding and DiscoverPID therefore depend on defaultLiveCWD resolving EXACTLY ONE live non-service hermes process. Any second interactive hermes session on the machine makes it ambiguous, defaultLiveCWD returns "", and the pid_bind phase plus the project link would go missing.

model/cost deliberately unpinned: which model the recording sees depends on the config.yaml in whatever HERMES_HOME the run exports. The maintainer's home defaults to model.default=gpt-5.6-luna, which irrlicht's capacity table DOES price (verified: EstimateCostUSD(gpt-5.6-luna, 16269, 5) = 0.00326, context window 1050000); the alternative local default google/gemma-4-26b-a4b is unpriced and would yield cost 0. Only tokens_nonzero is asserted; record should fill observations.model from the recording and add cost_nonzero if the recorded model is priced.

The onboarding rig has no hermes-specific env wiring today — grep for HERMES_HOME across tools/onboarding-factory/scripts returns nothing — so the driver and the recording daemon must be given a matching HERMES_HOME out of band.

sources.note: ParseLine: role='user' → user_message (ClearToolNames); role='assistant' + finish_reason='stop' → turn_done. finish_reason is the explicit turn boundary — no idle-flush seam is needed to settle to ready.

reconcile() emits EventNewSession on first sight and EventActivity when message_count grows, with Terminal = turnIsDone(); turnIsDone reads the newest active=1 row and is true only for role='assistant' AND finish_reason='stop'.

querySessionMetrics: TotalTokens = sessions.input_tokens + output_tokens (aggregate maintained by Hermes); cost priced via capacity alias table, deliberately not from sessions.estimated_cost_usd (subscription_included reports 0.0).
Source = ProcessOwnedStore over $HERMES_HOME/state.db (PathForPID ignores the pid — one shared store); observe-kind permission 'store' gates every read.

hermes gets BOTH the store watcher (line 90-91) and a processlifecycle scanner with the CommandPattern matcher + ExcludeArgv filter (line 102-110) — the scanner is what mints the transient proc-<PID> pre-session that carries the ready birth.

Live store, queried read-only (sqlite3 file:…?mode=ro). Session 20260802_212608_1dc71a is a literal basic turn: user 'Say only: beta' → assistant finish_reason='stop' 'beta', input_tokens=16269 output_tokens=5 message_count=2, model gpt-5.6-luna. Store-wide: 29 assistant/stop rows, 29 assistant/tool_calls, 30 user, 29 tool; cwd empty on 21/22 cli sessions and 0/3 tui sessions.
`hermes --version` → Hermes Agent v0.19.0 (2026.7.20) · upstream 177f1d7c; install dir /Users/ingo/hermes-local/.hermes/hermes-agent, Python 3.11.13.

DRIVE_ELICITS="send slash sleep wait_turn" (line 113) — every step this recipe needs is ported. wait_turn (line 258) polls COUNT(*) of assistant rows with finish_reason='stop' for the bound session; resolve_session_id binds only to a session started after the slot's launch timestamp, so a stale row in the shared store cannot satisfy it.
Sibling ProcessOwnedStore cell; its unpinned session_birth + same_session_as chaining is the anchoring template reused here for the same pre-session reason.

preconditions: hermes v0.19.0+ on PATH and a provider configured in <HERMES_HOME>/config.yaml with credentials, so a single prompt completes without an auth prompt
HERMES_HOME exported to the SAME recording home for both the driver and the recording daemon (the rig has no hermes env wiring today), so the daemon polls the store the run actually writes
sqlite3 on PATH — the driver's wait_turn reads the store directly; without it the driver spins to its deadline

no OTHER interactive hermes session live during the run: source='cli' rows carry no cwd, so the adapter's live-process CWD fallback needs exactly one non-service hermes process to bind the project and discover the PID
irrlichd recording with the hermes store watcher enabled and the 'store' permission granted (IRRLICHT_PERMISSION_MODE=grant-all on a fresh home)
setup: The interactive driver launches `hermes chat` under tmux in a fresh per-run cwd and polls the pane for 'Type your message or /help' before typing — the TUI swallows keystrokes sent during its ~seconds-long boot

Hermes writes no transcript file: the slot's transcript path is '<store>?session=<id>', the same encoding the watcher puts on agent.Event.TranscriptPath, and the session id is resolved from the sessions table after the first send (the row does not exist at launch)
The prompt is a one-word reply request, so the turn carries no tool call (tool_calls_max: 0) and the session never enters waiting
timeout_seconds is 240 because the driver's deadline starts BEFORE the REPL boot poll (up to 60s) and the turn itself runs against a remote reasoning model

script.text: Reply with exactly the word: ok

verify: events.jsonl contains a session born in ready shortly after launch (expected to be the transient proc-<PID> pre-session; the store row does not exist until the first user message)
events.jsonl contains a state_transition → working when the prompt is sent
events.jsonl contains a state_transition → ready on the SAME session once the assistant row lands with finish_reason='stop'
no state_transition to waiting appears at any point (no tool call, no permission gate)
the session's recorded metrics carry non-zero cum_input+output tokens
the session's final live state is ready
